title: Android 17 is the first since 3.x to add new APIs without releasing to the AOSP
summary: Android 17 is the first version since 3.x to introduce new APIs without releasing them to the Android Open Source Project (AOSP), representing a significant shift in Google's closed-source approach to Android development that impacts custom ROMs and privacy-focused forks like GrapheneOS.
problem_solved: Raises concerns about transparency and open-source accessibility in Android development, affecting third-party developers' ability to understand and build upon new OS features.
why_valuable: Highlights the growing trend of proprietary APIs in Android, which undermines the open-source nature of the platform and creates challenges for independent OS maintainers.
